text:
Paint a sunset over green hills in this p5 sketch:
```javascript
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 400, WEBGL);
  brush.scaleBrushes(2);
  noLoop();
}

function draw() {
  translate(-width / 2, -height / 2);
  background("#f4efe4");
  // painting goes here
  fill(#87ceeb, 0.7)
  circle(200, 200, 150)
  fill(#87ceeb, 0.3)
  circle(200, 200, 70)
  fill(#87ceeb, 0.25)
  circle(200, 200, 35)
  fill(#87ceeb, 0.25)
  circle(200, 200, 50)
  fill(#87ceeb, 0.3)
  circle(180, 100, 45)
  fill("#b9c1a2", 0.7)
  circle(150, 110, 20)
  fill("#87ceeb", 0.4)
  circle(165, 115, 20)
  fill("#87ceeb", 0.6)
  circle(130, 105, 35)
  fill("#87ceeb", 0.7)
  circle(135, 110, 20)
  fill("#87ceeb", 0.55)
  circle(110, 110, 30)
  fill("#87ceeb", 0.45)
  circle(90, 105, 30)
  fill("#87ceeb", 0.3)
  circle(100, 110, 20)
  fill("#87ceeb", 0.6)
  circle(90, 115, 35)
  fill("#87ceeb", 0.7)
  circle(75, 115, 15)
}
```

text:
For watercolours:
- blush = brown
- skies = white with a blanc manger (magenta) colour in the atmosphere
- ground = green like an atypical pine forest
- hill = green
- pines = a lot of green trees

Brush the skies first with a big red ball. Then brush the trees with a grass pencil on top of a landscape. Then paint the hills with a bright greens paint on top of the tree pencil's green. 

For some more depth in the painting, brush the wind with a small brush on the lower hills. 

You can also paint the sunset with a bright yellow color by brush stroke that overlaps the hills.
